movesets.name: Mixed Utility
movesets.description: Mixed Dialga is an excellent utility Pokemon, thanks to its excellent bulk and typing letting it handle Pokemon like Giratina, Magearna, and Palkia-O. Heavy Slam deals heavy damage to Zacian and Hatterene thanks to Dialga's massive weight while also not being affected by Draco Meteor's Special Attack drop. Stealth Rock allows Dialga to aid its teammates, passively chipping their checks. Dragon Tail allows Dialga to stop sweeps from Pokemon like Roaring Moon and Calm Mind Arceus formes, but Roar can be opted for instead, as it ignores Substitutes from Cyclizar and Palkia-O and can phaze Fairy-types like Zacian and Magearna. Tera Flying grants a resistance to both of Dialga's weaknesses, Fighting and Ground, letting it check threats it otherwise couldn't like Great Tusk and Zamazenta-C, though this comes at the cost of increased damage from Stealth Rock. Dialga pairs well with Pokemon like Chi-Yu and Kyurem-W, which can beat many of its checks like Great Tusk, Landorus, and Zamazenta-C. Dialga checks Pokemon like Deoxys, Spectrier, and Hatterene, making it an excellent teammate for Pokemon weak to these threats like Palkia-O, Giratina, and Mewtwo. Dialga is also a solid phazer, with entry hazard setters like Skarmory and Magearna appreciating it forcing foes to take repeated bouts of chip damage from their hazards.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description: Although it suffers major competition from Magearna and Solgaleo for the Steel-type slot, Dialga's great typing, decent bulk, and useful utility options make it a good wall in Ubers UU. Earth Power gives Dialga a way to hit opposing Steel-types like Solgaleo and Magearna as well as Pokemon like Arceus-Poison and Hatterene, but Thunder Wave is an option to cripple Pokemon attempting to set up on it like Mewtwo, Zacian, and Zamazenta-C. Stealth Rock grants Dialga extra utility, giving Pokemon like Kyurem-W a difficult time switching in. Roar allows Dialga to phaze Pokemon attempting to set up like Sneasler and Zacian while also going through Substitutes from Palkia-O and Cyclizar, but Dragon Tail can phaze Taunt users like Arceus-Dark at the cost of not going through Substitute and being walled by Fairy-types like Hatterene and Magearna. If phazing is not a priority, Heavy Slam can be opted as a secondary STAB move, as it targets Pokemon like Hatterene and Kyurem-W. Tera Flying allows Dialga to flip the matchup against Pokemon like Great Tusk and Landorus and remove all of its weaknesses, although it does give Dialga a weakness to Stealth Rock. Spikes setters like Ogerpon-H can make Dialga's phazing more potent. Dialga struggles against strong physically offensive threats like Zacian, Kingambit, and Palafin, so physically defensive walls like Toxapex and Great Tusk that can take these Pokemon on make great partners. Offensive threats like Deoxys and Choice Scarf Kyurem-W appreciate Dialga crippling switch-ins with Stealth Rock and Thunder Wave.

movesets.name: Trick Room Setter
movesets.description: Dialga is an excellent pick on Trick Room teams due to its blend of low Speed, sky-high Special Attack, high Base Power moves, and ability to set Trick Room for itself. Draco Meteor does huge damage to Pokemon like Palkia-O and Kyurem-W, while also activating Dialga's Eject Pack, allowing it to bring in a threatening teammate like Ursaluna or Hoopa-U. Earth Power gives Dialga coverage to hit Steel-types like non-Air Balloon Gholdengo, opposing Dialga, and Magearna. Trick Room allows Dialga to outspeed almost every opposing Pokemon while also providing support to teammates like Solgaleo and Kingambit. Eject Pack allows Dialga to switch out when it drops its own stats with Draco Meteor, which lets it bring a teammate like Kingambit in safely. Tera Flying is used so Dialga can flip its only two weaknesses, Fighting and Ground, to a resistance and an immunity, making it much better against Zamazenta-C, Great Tusk, and Landorus, allowing it to set up Trick Room in front of these threats. Dialga sets Trick Room, making it a natural ally to Pokemon like Ursaluna, Kingambit, and Hoopa-U, which it can wallbreak alongside. As a Trick Room setter, it struggles with Pokemon like Taunt Arceus formes and phazers like Dialga, Giratina, and bulky Arceus formes. This means it pairs well with Pokemon like Ursaluna and Hoopa-U, which can break through these obstacles with sheer power, or Fairy-types like Magearna and Zacian, which are immune to Dragon Tail. Other Trick Room setters Dialga is commonly paired with, like Solgaleo and Hatterene, are great partners too, as they can set Trick Room for it, and Hatterene is especially good at this due to being immune to Taunt and phazing.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
• Dialga's unique typing and good offensive stats give it a niche as a strong wallbreaker that is also able to soft check Pokemon such as Primal Kyogre, Eternatus, Palkia-O, and utility Arceus formes. However, its middling Speed and weakness to common Ground-types such as Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground mean Dialga can struggle to get into a game safely, especially without reliable recovery; it also faces heavy competition from Eternatus and Palkia-O as a powerful attacker in bulky offense and balance teams alike.
  • Trick allows Dialga to cripple switch-ins such as Ho-Oh, Zygarde, Ferrothorn, and Chansey, allowing its teammates to break through the opposing team much more easily.
  • Draco Meteor is Dialga's strongest attack, being able to 2HKO defensive Primal Groudon, offensive Primal Kyogre, and utility Arceus formes and OHKO offensive Primal Groudon, Zygarde-C, and specially offensive Yveltal.
  • Fire Blast allows Dialga to OHKO Zacian-C on the switch and 2HKO defensive Necrozma-DM, preventing the latter from being a reliable switch-in.
  • Thunder hits defensive Primal Kyogre, Arceus-Water, and Ho-Oh for great damage while preventing Arceus-Fairy or Zacian-C from switching in reliably, unlike Draco Meteor. Flash Cannon prevents Fairy-types from walling Dialga, being able to OHKO Arceus-Fairy after Stealth Rock, thus preventing Dialga from being setup fodder for it while also being able to break through Tera Fairy Eternatus and Zygarde variants; however, it is generally less desirable, since it lets Ho-Oh come into Dialga more often.
  • The given EV spread avoids the 2HKO from Tera Normal Extreme Speed from Arceus and Arceus-Fairy's uninvested Judgment while always outspeeding Adamant Necrozma-DM.
  • Tera Dragon not only removes Dialga's weakness to Ground- and Fighting-type attacks but also pushes Draco Meteor's damage to new heights, being able to OHKO Extreme Killer Arceus, utility Arceus formes, and defensive Yveltal while also being able to 2HKO defensive Primal Kyogre and offensive Necrozma-DM.
  • Dialga is quite prediction reliant, so spamming Draco Meteor is heavily discouraged, as it can turn Dialga into setup fodder, especially if there are Steel- or Fairy-types on the opposing team. Double switching against predicted switch-ins such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM into checks such as Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh can maintain the team's momentum while keeping the pressure Dialga brings on defensive backbones. Using Trick can also be somewhat difficult, since Arceus formes barring Extreme Killer, Zacian-C, and Z-Move Necrozma-DM can stop it. Therefore, Trick should mostly be used against more passive and slower teams, such as stall, against Pokemon Dialga would typically come in on like defensive Yveltal, defensive Eternatus, Ferrothorn, and Alomomola.
  • Dialga typically fits on balance and bulky offense structures that appreciate its offensive and defensive capabilities while not worrying about its mediocre Speed tier. It appreciates teammates that can setup entry hazards so it can reach important damage thresholds such as OHKOing Arceus-Fairy after Stealth Rock with Flash Cannon. Teammates such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and utility Arceus formes are good for this; the former also appreciates Dialga briefly checking Primal Kyogre for it. Ground-type switch-ins such as Giratina-O, Ho-Oh, and Yveltal are great partners to handle Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground, with all three also being good switch-ins to Marshadow, which can threaten Dialga with Low Kick. Zygarde is also a good switch-in to Marshadow and Primal Groudon while offering Glare support to help Dialga handle faster threats such as Zacian-C or Palkia-O.
  • Strong special attackers such as Primal Kyogre, Eternatus, and Calm Mind Arceus formes like Dialga crippling special walls like Ho-Oh or Chansey so they can clear through teams much more easily. Strong physical attackers such as Primal Groudon, Marshadow, and Zacian-C also appreciate Dialga smashing through physical walls like Zygarde, Primal Groudon, Arceus-Dark, and Dondozo, while they can help overwhelm the defensive backbone of many balance teams.
